title: No sin too great for mercy—except the sin against the Holy Spirit
source_text: III. Vice versa vero docent nullum esse peccatum tam grave & tam atrox, quod veniam a Dei misericordia consequi non possit, mediante peccatoris fide & poenitentia: Excepto solum peccato, quod vocant in Spiritum Sanctum. Quo nomine intelligunt totalem, & ultroneam atque deliberatam, ex destinata malitia, divinae veritatis semel agnitae & gustatae abjectionem. Quod peccatum, nec in hoc, nec in futuro saeculo remittitur: Propterea quod impossibile est, qui in tale peccatum lapsi sunt renovari ad poenitentiam; juxta doctrinam Apostoli Heb. 6.
pass_a_gloss: Conversely they teach that there is no sin so grave and so atrocious that it cannot obtain pardon from God’s mercy, through the sinner’s faith and repentance: except only the sin which they call against the Holy Spirit. By which name they understand a total, and voluntary and deliberate, rejection from destined malice of divine truth once known and tasted. Which sin is remitted neither in this nor in the age to come: because it is impossible that those who have fallen into such a sin be renewed unto repentance; according to the Apostle’s teaching in Hebrews 6.
pass_b_english: Faith and repentance open mercy for any atrocity—save the sin against the Spirit.
That sin means deliberate, malicious casting off of known truth; Hebrews 6 says renewal to repentance is impossible.
